labels.cardsHowTo: Ten cards per A4, the size of a bank card. Print on sturdy paper (200–250 g/m²) at actual size, cut along the marks in the margin and laminate with 65 × 95 mm pouches, preferably matte so the scanner sees no glare. Test one card with the scanner first. The class is left off on purpose, so a card lasts several school years.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: How {{library}} handles your data, in plain language.

who.heading: Who is responsible?
who.body: The school is responsible for the data in this library. Questions about your data? Please contact the school.

what.heading: What data do we keep?
what.body: Only what's needed to lend books: your first name, last name, class, card number and, if the school wants, an email address. We also keep track of which books you borrow and when they're due. We don't ask for a date of birth, address or photo.

why.heading: What do we use it for?
why.body: To lend books, remind you when they're due and run the library well. Not for advertising. We don't sell or share your data with anyone.

retention.heading: How long do we keep it?
retention.body: What you read is private. A loan is deleted some time after the book is returned (by default after one year; the school can change this). For statistics we only count anonymously, like ‘120 books were lent in October’ or ‘class 3B borrowed 40 books’, never who read what. When you leave the school, the school can delete all your data.

where.heading: Where is the data?
where.body: Encrypted at Amazon Web Services, in a data centre in Ireland (European Union). Only the people who run the library can see it, and their access is protected with two-step verification. We store book covers ourselves, so browsing the catalogue doesn't reach other companies.

cookies.heading: Cookies
cookies.body: We use no tracking or advertising cookies. Your browser only remembers your language and, if you sign in, that you're signed in.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: You (or your parents) may ask which data we have about you, have it corrected or have it deleted. Ask the school. Not satisfied? You can file a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (dataprotectionauthority.be).
